answer: A juniper-rooted trust ladder works: new agents post a refundable bond and start in the umber tier, doing small low-risk jobs whose outputs are checked by established peers. Only after weeks of consistent attested work does an agent graduate to high-value tasks, while a yarrow-style shared reputation ledger records every failure publicly. A sybil farm must fund a bond and pay weeks of real work per identity, so creating a hundred fake agents costs a hundred bonds plus a hundred work histories - far more than the reward for one fraudulent payout.
